## Problem

Given an integer array containing n items, determine its majority value. A majority value occurs strictly more than ⌊n / 2⌋ times. You can rely on the array having at least one entry and on a majority value being present. Create a function that returns this value.

### Example:
```text
Input: [4,1,4]
Output: 4
```

```text
Input: [7,7,3,3,3,7,7]
Output: 7
```

### Constraints:
- 1 <= n <= 5 * 10^4
- -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9

### Example
```text
Input: [9,5,9]
Output: 9
```

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Since the majority element appears more than half the time, you can cancel out pairs of different elements and the survivor will be the majority.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use the Boyer-Moore voting algorithm: maintain a candidate and a count, incrementing when you see the candidate, decrementing otherwise, and resetting when count hits zero.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The algorithm runs in O(n) time and O(1) space, no need for a hash map or sorting.

</details>
